emergency.title: This may be a stroke. Get help now.
emergency.subtitle: Every minute matters. Get emergency care immediately.
emergency.unverifiedNote: Go to the nearest hospital now. Our team is still verifying the emergency phone number.
emergency.noteTime: Note the time the signs started
emergency.whyTime: Tell the doctor when the signs started. It helps them choose the right treatment.
emergency.fast.f.title: Face drooping
emergency.fast.f.desc: One side of the face droops or feels numb. Ask the person to smile.
emergency.fast.a.title: Arm or leg weakness
emergency.fast.a.desc: One arm or leg is weak or numb. Ask the person to raise both arms.
emergency.fast.s.title: Speech trouble
emergency.fast.s.desc: Speech is slurred or strange, or the person cannot understand. Ask them to repeat a simple sentence.
emergency.fast.t.title: Time to call
emergency.fast.t.desc: If you see any of these signs, get emergency care immediately.
emergency.step1: Get emergency care immediately: call for an ambulance, or go to the nearest hospital with 24-hour emergency care.
emergency.step2: Note the time the signs started and tell the doctor.
emergency.step3: Do not give food, drink or medicine unless a health worker says so.
emergency.step4: Stay with the person and keep them calm and safe.
emergency.step5: If they are unconscious but breathing, place them on their side.
emergency.chestPain: Chest pain or trouble breathing? Call emergency now.

about.title: About this check
about.subtitle: It takes about 3 minutes.
about.anonymous: Anonymous: we never ask for your name or phone number.
about.notDiagnosis: This is not a medical diagnosis. It helps you decide what to do next.
about.time: Part 1 has 8 short questions. Part 2 is optional and makes your plan personal.
about.consentHelp: Only age group, sex and result level are counted, to help health programs plan. No name, no phone number. You can change this any time in Profile.
family.toggle: I am checking for a parent or relative.
family.toggleHelp: The questions will be worded for the other person, and the result and card will say who it is for.
family.whoHelp: Do not write a full name. A word like “Mother” is enough.
q.Q0: Right now, does anyone have: face drooping, weakness or numbness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking or understanding, sudden vision loss, sudden loss of balance, or a sudden very bad headache?
q.Q1.family: How old is the person you are checking for?
q.Q1.label: Age
q.Q2.family: Is the person male or female?
q.Q2.pregnantMessage: Blood pressure in pregnancy needs care from your antenatal provider. Please ask them.
q.Q3.self: Have you ever had a stroke or a “mini-stroke” (TIA)?
q.Q3.family: Has the person ever had a stroke or a “mini-stroke” (TIA)?
q.Q4.self: When was your blood pressure last checked?
q.Q4.family: When was their blood pressure last checked?
q.Q4.help: “I don't know” is a normal answer. 3 in 10 adults in Cambodia have never been checked.
q.Q5.self: Do you know your latest blood pressure numbers?
q.Q5.family: Do you know their latest blood pressure numbers?
q.Q5.help: Look at the paper or the machine screen from the last check. Choose “I don't know” if you are not sure.
q.Q5.pictureAlt: Example blood pressure machine showing 128 over 82
q.Q6.self: Do you take medicine for high blood pressure, or has a doctor told you your blood pressure is high?
q.Q6.family: Does the person take medicine for high blood pressure, or has a doctor told them their blood pressure is high?
q.Q6.help: Answer Yes if either is true.
q.Q7.self: Has a doctor ever told you that you have diabetes?
q.Q7.family: Has a doctor ever told the person that they have diabetes?
q.Q8.self: Do you smoke or chew tobacco?
q.Q8.family: Does the person smoke or chew tobacco?
q.Q8.help: Chewing betel with tobacco counts as tobacco.
q.Q9.self: What is your height and weight?
q.Q9.family: What is their height and weight?
q.Q9.help: We use these to work out BMI (body mass index). Choose “I don't know” if you are not sure.
q.Q10.self: In the last 30 days, did you drink 6 or more alcoholic drinks on one occasion?
q.Q10.family: In the last 30 days, did the person drink 6 or more alcoholic drinks on one occasion?
q.Q11.self: Did your mother, father, brother or sister have a stroke?
q.Q11.family: Did the person's mother, father, brother or sister have a stroke?
q.Q12.self: Do you often add salt, fish sauce or soy sauce to your food?
q.Q12.family: Does the person often add salt, fish sauce or soy sauce to their food?
q.Q12.help: Count salt, fish sauce, soy sauce, prahok and seasoning powder.
q.Q13.self: Is your daily work mostly sitting, light movement, or heavy physical work?
q.Q13.family: Is the person's daily work mostly sitting, light movement, or heavy physical work?
q.Q13.help: This does not change the risk level. It helps us choose exercise advice.

plan.lower.headline: Lower risk. Keep it up.
plan.lower.1: Check your blood pressure at least once a year from age 40.
plan.lower.2: Exercise: aim for 150 minutes a week (for example 30 minutes on 5 days). Brisk walking, cycling and farm work all count.
plan.lower.2sitting: Your work is mostly sitting: stand and walk for 5 minutes every hour.
plan.lower.3: Keep salt under 5 g a day (about one level teaspoon in total, counting fish sauce, soy sauce and seasoning powder).
plan.lower.4: Eat 5 servings of fruit and vegetables a day (about 400 g).
plan.lower.5: No tobacco. Never drink 6 or more drinks on one occasion.
plan.lower.6: Learn FAST and share the FAST card with your family.
plan.moderate.headline: Moderate risk. Act in the next 4 weeks.
plan.moderate.1: Get your blood pressure measured within 2 weeks at a health centre or a pharmacy that checks it. Ask also about blood sugar and cholesterol checks.
plan.moderate.1skip: You were measured in the last month, so you can skip this step.
plan.moderate.2: Exercise plan: weeks 1–2, a 10-minute walk after one meal a day; weeks 3–4, 20 minutes on 5 days; by week 6, 150 minutes a week.
plan.moderate.2heavy: Your heavy physical work already counts as exercise, so focus on salt, tobacco and blood pressure instead.
plan.moderate.3: Pick up to 3 goals from your biggest factors and tick them off each week.
plan.moderate.4: If the check shows 140/90 or higher, see a health worker for a plan. Do not treat yourself.
plan.moderate.5: Do not start or stop any medicine on your own.
plan.moderate.6: Do this check again in 3 months.
plan.higher.headline: Higher risk. Please see a health worker within 1 week.
plan.higher.1: Choose a place and go within 7 days (use Find Care, then call).
plan.higher.2: Take the check-up card. Ask for a blood pressure check, blood sugar and cholesterol tests, whether you need medicine, and help to stop tobacco.
plan.higher.3: If you already take blood pressure medicine, keep taking it exactly as prescribed, even if you feel well.
plan.higher.4: Until you are seen: cut salt, no tobacco, no heavy drinking. A gentle 10–15 minute walk is fine if you have no chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness. Do not start new hard exercise.
plan.higher.5: Tell your family and show them FAST.
plan.higher.6: Follow-up: on day 3 and day 7, mark in Current Health whether you have seen a health worker.
plan.today.headline: Your blood pressure is very high. Please get checked today.
plan.today.1: Go to a health facility today. The nearest places are shown above.
plan.today.2: If there is any warning sign (headache, vision change, weakness, confusion, chest pain), go to the Emergency screen now.
plan.today.warningButton: I see a warning sign: Emergency
plan.prior.headline: You have had a stroke before. Please follow your doctor's plan.
plan.prior.4: Know FAST, and make sure your family knows it too.

goal.vegetables: 5 servings of fruit and vegetables a day
salt.tip.1: Taste food before adding salt, fish sauce or soy sauce.
salt.tip.2: Use less dipping sauce, or mix it with lime juice and water.
salt.tip.3: Add flavour with lime, lemongrass, garlic, chilli and herbs instead of seasoning powder.
salt.tip.4: Eat salted fish, prahok, instant noodles and pickles less often.

learn.title: Learn
learn.subtitle: Simple facts to help you prevent stroke and act fast.
learn.fast.title: FAST: the warning signs of stroke
learn.fast.intro: A stroke happens suddenly. If you see any of these signs, get emergency care immediately.
learn.fast.other: Other sudden signs: numbness, confusion, vision loss, loss of balance, a very bad headache.
learn.fast.shareTitle: StrokeSafe: know the signs of stroke (FAST)
learn.fast.copied: The FAST card text was copied. Paste it into a message.
learn.fast.failed: Sharing is not available on this device.
learn.bp.title: How to measure blood pressure
learn.bp.intro: Raised blood pressure is the main stroke risk you can control. Many people feel well and do not know it is high.
learn.bp.step.1: Do not smoke, drink coffee or exercise for 30 minutes before.
learn.bp.step.2: Sit quietly for 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat on the floor.
learn.bp.step.3: Put the cuff on your bare upper arm. Rest the arm on a table at heart level.
learn.bp.step.4: Do not talk while the machine measures.
learn.bp.step.5: Take two readings, one minute apart. Write both down with the date.
learn.bp.step.6: Ask a health worker what your numbers mean for you.
learn.bp.read: The top number (SYS) is pressure when the heart beats. The bottom number (DIA) is pressure between beats. 140/90 or higher is raised: see a health worker for a plan.
learn.salt.title: Salt guide
learn.salt.intro: Adults in Cambodia eat about 9.5 g of salt a day on average (STEPS 2023). The WHO limit is under 5 g, about one level teaspoon in total.
learn.habits.title: Healthy habits
learn.habits.item.1: Move for 150 minutes a week, for example 30 minutes on 5 days. Brisk walking, cycling and farm work all count.
learn.habits.item.2: Eat 5 servings of fruit and vegetables a day (about 400 g).
learn.habits.item.3: No tobacco: smoking and chewing both raise stroke risk.
learn.habits.item.4: Never drink 6 or more alcoholic drinks on one occasion.
learn.habits.item.5: If your work is mostly sitting, stand and walk for 5 minutes every hour.
learn.prevention.title: Stroke prevention
learn.prevention.intro: Stroke is the leading cause of death in Cambodia. Many strokes can be prevented.
learn.prevention.item.1: Know your blood pressure, and have it checked at least once a year from age 40.
learn.prevention.item.2: If a health worker gives you medicine, take it exactly as prescribed. Do not start or stop medicine on your own.
learn.prevention.item.3: Ask about blood sugar and cholesterol checks.
learn.prevention.item.4: Teach your family FAST, so they can act quickly.
